issues.detail: The Hebrew subject is second-person plural ('you said'), but the Chinese renders it as third-person feminine plural ('她們卻說'). This changes who is speaking.
The Hebrew 'נָנוּס' (we will flee) is first-person plural, but the Chinese renders it as second-person plural ('你們必騎馬逃竄'), changing the subject from 'we' to 'you'.
The Hebrew 'נִרְכָּב' (we will ride) is first-person plural, but the Chinese renders it as second-person plural ('你們必騎輕騎的馬'), again changing the subject.
